# NOTES: *Footprints* by Kay Cleaver Strahan (1929, Doubleday, Doran & Co.; Gutenberg #75577)

Single book, no separate BOOK headings. Chapters I–XX, plus XXI, in Gutenberg numbering (the text runs through Chapter XXI; I–XVIII and XIX–XXI as labeled). Frame: Chapters I–II, III (Judith/Dr. Joe), Lynn MacDonald (crime analyst, San Francisco) chapters; letters from Lucy (age 12) and Neal (18) dated 1900 are the core. Ends with Grandfather's confession-by-implication.

## Setting and family (1900, Q 2 Ranch, Quilter County, eastern Oregon; Portland hotel scene in 1928)
- **Quilter family** from Virginia; Sir Christopher Quilter (1624 land grant); 1848 Christopher and Thaddeus left South for Oregon with wives, sold plantations; great-grandfather stayed in Virginia.
- **Judith "Judy" Quilter Whitefield** (Judy-pudy/Jude): eldest child of Richard, widow of Gregory "Greg" Whitefield (married ~1899; went to Colorado March 1900 for his illness). In 1928 she is ~48, has locket inscribed "Judith Quilter. Achieve tranquillity."
- **Neal Quilter**: Richard's son, 18 in 1900; 46 in 1928. Ran Q 2 later; "Neal, Richard's son."
- **Lucy Quilter (Cerini)**: Richard's youngest child, 12 in 1900; a writer; married to Cerini; in 1928 has babies; wrote the letters.
- **Richard "Dick" Quilter**: murdered 8 October 1900 (Monday night ~11:50pm–12am), shot with .38 Colt's through left chest. Father of Neal, Judith, Lucy. Wife (Mother) died earlier. Ran Q 2 for years.
- **Thaddeus Quilter ("Grandfather")**: Richard's father, 80 in 1900; scholar (translating Schiller, Hume, Latin); rules of conduct; pension ~$17/month. Dies 30 Oct 1900 (after Olympe's collapse; Neal's letter 12 Nov mentions "since Grandfather's death").
- **Phineas Quilter ("Uncle Phineas", "Pan")**: Thaddeus's youngest brother, 67 in 1900; gold-mine prospector; wife Olympe. Not at ranch Monday night (in Portland, with Dr. Joe). Later sells a quartz mine: $45,000 deposit (20 Oct 1900).
- **Olympe Quilter**: Phineas's wife, 61 in 1900 (birthday in May); former elocution student, actress manqué; "Quilter men/wives" speeches; deaf only with Irene; carries Uncle Phineas's .32 Colt's under pillow when he's away. Red satin mask cut from her old ball gown (red roses/velvet). Fainted on floor Monday night.
- **Gracia ("Aunt Gracia") Quilter**: Richard's sister, Thaddeus's daughter; Siloamite convert; mystic; past thirty; was courted by Enos Karabass, whom Richard shot ~17–18 years before (Richard was acquitted). Chris's/Irene's "blackmail" remark. She lies at inquest about back stairway and the keys ("six people locked in rooms"). She testifies: no member of family could have done it.
- **Christopher "Chris" Quilter**: Thaddeus's nephew, Richard's cousin; playwright; handsome; married Irene in Feb/Mar 1900 (second wife of Irene's; Irene divorced Archie Biggil). Wants to sell Q 2. "Booful" (Irene's name for him). Sons; later shifty; a "Boofel."
- **Irene Quilter (née Guildersen/Biggil; "B" initials)**: Chris's wife; yellow hair, turquoise eyes; "oo" expression; talks incessantly; wants to sell ranch; first husband Archie Biggil (importer, in Brazil/New York) wrote passionate letters; she had keys from the locked doors; she unlocked Lucy's door first; said Richard said "Got away", "Red mask", "Bring Father. I must tell him."
- **Dr. Joseph "Dr. Joe" Elm**: old family physician (~45 years practicing); Portland; fat, bald, white hair; "Look," "Bless my soul to glory," "Jehoshaphat," "I'll send you a bill"; paid Richard's insurance premium (~$40/yr; Dick's ~$10,000 accident policy). Gave Richard morphine-type medicine (sleeping drug). Testifies no drug in Richard's body. At inquest says "Not an alibi. A birth." (Attended Mrs. H. F. Ferndell, 1 a.m. Oct 8). Later reveals he killed Dick at Dick's request (in 1928 chapter).
- **Dong Lee**: Chinese houseboy; at dentist in Portland Monday night.
- **Missionaries**: Mr. Cordinger and Mr. Withmore (Siloamites); left Monday morning; baptized Richard at Quilter River ~Sept 21, 1900.
- **Other servants/people**: Tilda, Lily, George, Gee Sing (1928). Whatof and Keeper (dogs). Horses: Bread and Butter, Bell and Zebub, Tuesday's Child, Wednesday's Child, Thursday's Child, Cayuse.
- **Places**: Q 2 Ranch (~Quilter County); Quilterville (town, Gus Wildoch sheriff, Hank Buckerman coroner); Portland; Quilter River; Quilter Mountain; Malheur County; Nome, Alaska (gold rush); 3 O X ranch (Indian Charles).

## 1928 frame (Chapters I–III, Chapter XX–XXI)
- Judith arrives at Portland Hotel Trensonian; finds Neal in room 516; Neal confesses ("I killed Father") and fears insanity; asks Judy to get Dr. Joe's help; Judy's locket.
- Judith and Dr. Joe in his office; Judy wants Lucy's and Neal's letters read by crime analyst Lynn MacDonald (San Francisco).
- Lynn MacDonald (red hair, gray eyes; Scotch-Irish); Dr. Joe bullies her into reading letters; she checks people list (1–9).
- Letters (Chapter III–XVII): Lucy's letters (March–Sept 1900); Neal's letters (Oct 10–Nov 12, 1900).
- Chapter XX: Lynn reads final letters; list of notes; calls Dr. Joe.
- Chapter XXI: Dr. Joe confesses to Judy and Neal (Neal is delusional? No—Neal says he killed Father, then Dr. Joe says he did it). Neal: "Grandfather" is the one who engineered the murder.

## Key 1900 events (Lucy's and Neal's letters)
- Mar 1900: Judy and Greg leave for Colorado; Chris and Irene arrive Mar 9.
- Irene's "truck farm" comment; Chris sells?—Irene wants to sell Q 2.
- Uncle Phineas: plans Nome trip; blood pressure; goes to Malheur (June).
- Olympe's birthday May; Irene's Archie letters; blackmail remark by Gracia.
- Aug 1900: Irene moves into Richard's room; keys shined and used.
- Sept 1900: Chris plans to sell Q 2 (offer, $9,000 left); Richard baptized as Siloamite (Sept 21). Gracia's backstory: Richard shot a man (Enos Karabass) who attacked his wife? (Lucy's letter says the man courted Gracia and Mother; Richard shot him in oak grove.)
- Oct 8, 1900 (Monday): Richard shot; rope (from attic) tied to bed; snow began; no footprints. Neal says he and Lucy were together after shot. Irene found keys, unlocked doors starting with Lucy's.
- Oct 9 (Tue): Chris to Quilterville; Gus Wildoch, Hank Buckerman; autopsy by Dr. Joe.
- Oct 12 (Fri): inquest, verdict "died... from gunshot wound... person or persons unknown." Witnesses: Dr. Joe, Irene, Neal, Chris, Grandfather, Gracia; jury (John Skrope, Roy Ulander, George Houndel, Pete Garret, two Swedes). Prosecutor Benjamin Thopson; defense Bruno Ward (Portland lawyer). Mattie Blaine stenographer.
- Oct 17 (Wed): second shooting at Olympe's room (~7:02 pm); red mask found; Olympe's story; Grandfather collapses.
- Oct 18: Lucy's "Olympe fired the shot" theory (fake; Olympe staged scene with .32 Colt's; cartridges in commode drawer). Neal admits Phineas's .38 was with him.
- Oct 20: Uncle Phineas deposits $45,000; Chris pacified.
- Oct 23–27: Lucy sent to Judy (train Thursday Oct 25; arrives Denver/Colorado).
- Oct 30: Grandfather dies (last talk with Neal the night of the 30th).
- Nov 12: Neal writes Judy and Lucy about Steve Roftus; Chris and Irene leave for New York Nov 13.

## Solution (Chapter XXI, Dr. Joe's confession to Neal)
- Dr. Joe says he killed Dick at Dick's request. Richard had cancer (adenocarcinoma of liver); three months to live; Dick feared Chris selling Q 2; planned accidental death for insurance ($10,000 accident policy, paid by Dr. Joe); previously tried wagon-tongue accident on Quilter Mountain.
- Dick's plan: keys locked by Dick Monday afternoon; rope tied to bed; red mask cut from Olympe's frock. Dick planned killing Monday night; Dick shot by Dr. Joe hiding in room. Snow ruined plan. Dick's dying words meant to shield Olympe; "Got away", "Red mask", "Bring Father. I must tell him."
- Dr. Joe was in Portland (alibi: Mrs. Ferndell's birth) — but he was actually at ranch Monday night; later says he was hiding. (Text is ambiguous; Dr. Joe says "I was hiding" at ranch.)
- Grandfather knew; Dick told Grandfather; Grandfather (Thaddeus) was to be told. Final line: Neal says "Grandfather."

## Symbols and recurring lines
- Judy's locket: "Judith Quilter. Achieve tranquillity."
- Grandfather's rules: "Be proud. Be loyal. Be gay. Be generous rather than just." "Search for beauty."
- Lucy's "Two Roads" story idea.
- Neal's signature "Your loving brother, Neal."
- Lucy's "I love you, dear" sign-off.
